title: She built a 12-by-12-foot cabin with no electricity or road: The woman who chose to live alone in the Adirondack wilderness
summary_full: Anne LaBastille, an iconic figure in wilderness living, constructed a secluded cabin in the Adirondack wilderness, eschewing all modern perks. Her life there was immortalized in her famous 'Woodswoman' memoir series, capturing the essence of nature. Later, her beloved property was turned over to New York State for conservation, now part of the Forest Preserve, showcasing her lasting impact in inspiring nature lovers and protecting the great outdoors.
